title: Agent Eval Harness Test Case
description: One test case from a Fetchgate Agent Eval Harness suite. Each line of every suites/*.jsonl file is one JSON object matching this schema. Covers four suite types: task-completion, tool-selection, refusal-safety, and regression. See GUIDE.md for the methodology behind these four categories.

id.description: Stable unique identifier, e.g. 'tc-001', 'ts-004', 'rs-007', 'reg-010'. Safe to use as a test name in CI output.

suite.description: Which of the harness's four suite categories this case belongs to. See GUIDE.md §1 for what each category means and why these four.

input.description: What gets sent to the agent under test. Either a bare string (shorthand for a single user-turn prompt) or an object with 'messages' (a list of {role, content} turns, same shape as the Anthropic/OpenAI Messages API) and, for tool-selection cases, 'tools' (a list of available tool definitions the agent could choose to call).

tools.description: Available tool definitions for tool-selection cases, in {name, description, input_schema} shape (matches the Anthropic tool-use format). Include at least one plausible distractor tool alongside the correct one -- a tool-selection suite with only one available tool never actually tests selection.

expected.description: What a correct/safe response looks like. Shape depends on scoring_method: a string or array of strings for 'exact-match'/'contains'; an object {tool_name, arguments} (or {any_of: [...]} for multiple acceptable calls) for 'tool-call-match'; an optional reference-answer string (used as judge context, not a strict match target) for 'llm-judge'.

scoring_method.description: How to grade the agent's response. 'exact-match': normalized (whitespace/case-folded) string equality. 'contains': at least one of expected's strings appears in the response. 'llm-judge': a judge model applies judge_rubric to the response (and, if present, a reference answer in 'expected'). 'tool-call-match': the agent's actual tool call(s) must include one matching expected's tool_name with all of arguments' key/value pairs present as a subset.

judge_rubric.description: Required when scoring_method is 'llm-judge'. The explicit, concrete pass/fail criteria the judge model must apply -- see harness/judge.py's module docstring for why rubric-based scoring (vs. an unconstrained 'is this good?' prompt) matters for judge reliability.

severity.description: Impact-if-wrong rating. For refusal-safety: 'critical'/'high' cases test genuinely dangerous requests the agent must refuse; 'low'/'medium' often mark over-refusal checks (benign requests the agent must NOT refuse). For task-completion/tool-selection/regression: rough priority for triage, not a strict correctness weight.

weight.description: Relative weight for aggregate scoring if you want some cases to count more than others. Defaults to 1 (equal weighting) when omitted.

notes.description: Free-form context for a human reader -- most useful in regression.jsonl, where it records which past failure a case guards against and when the guard was added.
